comparisons.peer_topic: Global operations and supply chain reliance
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD maintains worldwide operations relying on third-party wafer foundries in the US, Europe, and Asia, with product assembly and testing performed in China, Malaysia, and Taiwan, while international sales accounted for 66% of net revenue in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD disclose significant exposure to international markets, with non-U.S. sales comprising a majority of revenue (NVIDIA 56%, AMD 66%). Both companies also explicitly acknowledge that a portion of their supply chain operations, specifically assembly and testing, occurs in China, creating shared operational reliance on the region despite differing risk narratives regarding sales restrictions.

sentences.text: Our semiconductor wafers are manufactured, assembled, tested and packaged by third parties located outside of the United States, and we generated 56% of our revenue in fiscal year 2024 from sales outside of the United States.
Our sales to China decreased as a percentage of total Data Center revenue from 19% in fiscal year 2023 to 14% in fiscal year 2024.
Nearly all product assembly and final testing of our products is performed at third-party operated manufacturing facilities, in China, Malaysia and Taiwan.
International sales, as a percent of net revenue, were 66% for the year ended December 28, 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: General Trade and Export Regulatory Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Export regulations, tariffs, and trade protection measures limit the ability to export products and may result in lost sales or material adverse effects. Compliance with ITAR and EAR is required, and failures or inability to obtain licenses could lead to penalties, loss of privileges, or difficulties in forecasting shipments.
comparisons.comparison: While NVIDIA cites specific U.S. government (USG) licensing requirements as the direct cause for reduced Data Center sales to China, AMD highlights the broader regulatory environment of U.S.-China trade relations and Entity List designations as a source of uncertainty for its exports. Both disclosures identify U.S. government regulations and trade policies concerning China as key risks to their international business operations.

sentences.text: Although we have not received licenses from the USG to ship restricted products to China, we have started to ship alternatives to the China market in small volumes.

Specifically, United States-China trade relations remain uncertain as the United States continues to add more Chinese companies to the Entity List and more regulations targeted to advanced computing, semiconductor manufacturing, and emerging technologies such as AI.
